title: In Free Fall: A Thought Experiment on Vertical Perspective
author: Hito Steyerl
note: Read in its own right as an article. Steyerl's essay on groundlessness, the loss of the horizon line, the history and downfall of linear perspective, and the politics of the vertical/aerial (drone, satellite, God's-eye) view. Extends the existing Doomscroll/Steyerl cluster (PRs #5-#7) with the primary text those podcasts orbit.
summary: Argues that contemporary visual culture is 'in free fall': the stable horizon line that underwrote linear perspective (and with it a stable observer, calculable space, and linear progressive time) has given way to aerial/vertical views — Google Maps, satellite, drone, 3D cinema — that only simulate a stable ground for a distanced, superior spectator. Traces perspective from Alhazen and Uccello through Panofsky's critique, its complicity in colonialism/racial propaganda (Uccello's Miracle of the Desecrated Host), its 19th-c. destabilization in Turner (The Slave Ship, Rain Steam and Speed), to 20th-c. cinema/cubism and today's 'military-surveillance-entertainment complex' (Elsaesser) and vertical sovereignty (Weizman, Mbembe's necropolitics). Ends via Adorno: free fall as terror and liberation both — a groundlessness that can be new representational freedom and a 'radicalized class war from above.'
